name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step and no step uses anything unbought; reconciled line by line. No orphaned or invented ingredients.
No cost_lines were supplied in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-ounce, lasts-several-batches, or nothing-left claims; the only dollar figure is the ${cost_ps} token.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, elote, is one of those foods that ruins you a little. Once you have had corn with lime, cotija, and a creamy tangy dressing, plain buttered corn feels like it forgot to get dressed. The trouble is street corn on its own is a side, and a side does not pay your protein bill. So we built a whole dinner around it and let the corn ride shotgun.

Here is the deal. Seasoned chicken over cilantro lime rice, a big scoop of that street corn salad, avocado and red onion on top, one more squeeze of lime. It lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, which is exactly the neighborhood we want: real food, real protein, under 800 calories, and it tastes like you ordered it instead of prepped it.
prose.shop_smart:
This one shops easy because most of it is pantry and produce, not specialty stuff. A few honest moves:

  • Buy canned whole kernel corn and drain it well. The recipe was built on canned and drained, so you are not chasing fresh cobs or thawing frozen. Grab the cans and get on with your day.
  • Chicken breast is the engine of the plate. Buy the larger family pack of boneless skinless breast and cut your own 1-inch chunks. Cutting them yourself is the whole trick to even cooking.
  • Cotija shows up in two places, in the corn salad and sprinkled on top, so buy it once and portion it twice. Same story with the cilantro and the limes, which get spread across the rice, the salad, and the finish.
  • The spice rub is chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder. If those are already in your cabinet, this batch barely moves the receipt. If not, they are cheap and you will use them for months.
  • Greek yogurt and avocado oil mayonnaise carry the creamy tang. Plain Greek yogurt, nothing flavored, and you only need a modest amount so the tub goes a long way.
prose.make_it:
This is a four-part assembly: rice, corn salad, chicken, then build. Nothing here is hard, it just wants a little order.

  1. Cilantro lime rice. Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and the sea salt, cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer about 20 minutes until tender. While it cooks, stir the chopped cilantro together with lime juice and lime zest in a bowl. When the rice is warm, fold it into the cilantro lime mix and toss.
  2. Street corn salad. In a bowl combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the jalapeno if you are using it, cilantro, and the salt. Stir gently until it comes together, taste, and adjust. Set it aside so the flavors get acquainted.
  3. Season the chicken. Combine all the spices in a small bowl. Put the chicken chunks in a larger bowl and toss until every piece is coated.
  4. Cook the chicken. Add the olive oil to a large skillet over medium heat. Once it is hot, add the chicken and cook about 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and the internal temp hits 165 degrees F. Do not crowd the pan, work in batches if you need to.
  5. Build the base. Divide the warm cilantro lime rice among your containers and spread it out a little so there is room for toppings.
  6. Top it off. Add the chicken chunks, a generous scoop of the street corn salad, then the avocado, red onion, a little more cilantro, a sprinkle of crumbled cotija, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
prose.portion_html:
This batch is built for 14 containers, so think in even scoops, not eyeballing. Split the cilantro lime rice across all 14 first as your base layer, then lay the chicken on top so every box gets its fair share of the protein. The street corn salad goes on as a generous scoop per box.

Hold the fresh stuff back if you are prepping ahead. Avocado, red onion, the extra cotija, and that final squeeze of lime are best added the day you eat, not the day you cook, so they stay bright. Everything lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a container, which is the whole reason we do it this way.
prose.cost_closing_html: Here is what makes this one a keeper for the wallet. Chicken breast, rice, canned corn, and a handful of spices are about as budget-friendly as a real dinner gets, and the yogurt and cotija stretch flavor a lot further than their price suggests. At ${cost_ps} a serving you are eating something that tastes like a food-truck order for less than the drink would have cost you there.
prose.upsell_html: Fourteen containers of street corn chicken bowls in the fridge means fourteen decisions you already made. steps: Make the cilantro lime rice: bring the water to a boil, add rice and sea salt, cover, reduce heat to low and simmer about 20 minutes until tender. Stir chopped cilantro with lime juice and zest in a bowl, then fold in the warm rice and toss.

Make the street corn salad: combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, jalapeno if using, cilantro, and salt. Stir gently, taste, adjust seasoning, and set aside.
Season the chicken: combine all the spices in a small bowl, then toss the chicken chunks in a larger bowl until fully coated.
Cook the chicken: add olive oil to a large skillet over medium heat, then cook the chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side until cooked through and the internal temp reaches 165 degrees F.
Build the base: divide the warm cilantro lime rice among the containers and spread it out to make room for toppings.
Top the bowls: add the chicken, a generous scoop of street corn salad, then avocado, red onion, more cilantro, a sprinkle of cotija, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
